quote: Suppose that Vj has the MoD with parameter δj for j = 1, 2. Let Hj(v; δj) be the CDF and hj(v; δj) be the PDF of Vj. Then V1 is said to be stochastically smaller than V2 with respect to likelihood ratio order (say V1 ≤lr V2), if h1(v;δ1)/h2(v;δ2) is a decreasing function ∀ v values. The likelihood ratio ordering is as follows: h1(v;δ1)/h2(v;δ2) = [δ1³(v+1)²e^{−δ1v}/(δ1(δ1+2)+2)] · [(δ2(δ2+2)+2)/(δ2³(v+1)²e^{−δ2v})]. Then, for δ2 < δ1, we obtain d/dv log[h1(v;δ1)/h2(v;δ2)] < 0 ∀v ≥ 0. So, d/dv log[h1(v;δ1)/h2(v;δ2)] is decreasing in v and consequently V1 ≤lr V2.
